marker.description: green painted mark on the distal end of the bone

main_explanation: The specimen is an isolated radius, a long bone of the forearm. Its characteristic distal end, including the styloid process, identifies it.

supporting_question.question: What clinical condition commonly arises from damage to the pointed part of this bone (the radial styloid process)?
supporting_question.explanation: A Colles fracture is a common fracture of the distal radius, typically occurring about 2.5 cm proximal to the radiocarpal joint, often involving the radial styloid process and resulting in dorsal displacement of the distal fragment.

true_false.statement: The radial styloid process is located medial to the ulnar styloid process.
true_false.explanation: The radial styloid process is located on the lateral side of the distal radius, while the ulnar styloid process is on the medial side of the distal ulna.
